items.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025
items.q: And so the guitar players like Bucky and George and those people didn’t have that feel.

ctx.x: Yes. Oh yeah. And usually if they had a guy singer or something that they had to put it in a different key, I have perfect pitch and so it was like having to transpose each note as I sight read it. But the musicians were incredible. Because it was, you know, after the big band era and so the people that were with big bands — Everett Barksdale — do you remember that guitar player with Art Tatum? Everett did a lot of demos. And then as it went on the newer kids, Al Gorgoni and Trade Martin, the younger kids came in…
feel to it. And so the guitar players like Bucky and George and those people didn’t have that feel. So the new young kids were playing it.

You know Bucky talked about that, how some people could grab the — they call it the “straight eighth note feel” as opposed to swing. Some people could transition to it and some people couldn’t or didn’t want to.
